# Fishers: prompt bank for review

Built from `content/` by `tools/build-prompts.js`, checked by `tools/verify.js` (every name and alias is found at its cited verse in the WEB or KJV) and `tools/validate.js` (game rules and matcher).

**How tiers are set.** *verses* is how many verses in the WEB and KJV use the answer's name or aliases. The most frequent ~5% become Mustard Seed, the next ~7.5% Five Loaves, the next ~20% Lost Coin, the rest Hidden Treasure. Answers marked *(manual)* were moved by hand, for names that are famous but rare in the text, or common words that inflate the count. Prompts whose answers are descriptions or book titles are tiered entirely by hand. The Lost Sheep and Best Seat are hand-picked. All tiers are estimates.

**Accepted spellings.** *Aliases* are found in the Bible text. *Forms* (modern names, labels) and *short* forms (abbreviations, which are only suggested) are not text-checked; they are listed here for review.

---

**🐑 The Lost Sheep:** 3 John. 3 John is the shortest book in the Bible by word count, a letter of about 220 words in Greek, written by the elder to Gaius (3 John 1).

**🪑 Best Seat:** Habakkuk. Habakkuk asks God how long the wicked will prosper, and ends by rejoicing even if the fig tree does not blossom (Habakkuk 1:2; 3:17–18).

- **Enoch, 1 Enoch, Jubilees, Jasher**: An ancient book, but not part of the 66-book canon.
- **Gospel of Thomas, Thomas, Gospel of Judas, Didache**: An early writing outside the Bible.
- **3 Corinthians, 3 Kings, 4 Kings, 3 Peter, 4 John**: No such book in the Bible.
- **Laodiceans**: Paul mentions a letter from Laodicea (Colossians 4:16), but it is not in the Bible.

### Near misses

- **Nathanael**: Many identify him with Bartholomew, but Scripture never says so directly (John 1:45–49).
- **Luke, Mark**: A Gospel writer, but the New Testament never calls him an apostle.
- **Timothy, Titus, Silas**: A trusted co-worker of Paul, but not called an apostle in so many words.
- **James the brother of Jesus, James the Just, James the Lord's brother**: Possibly: Galatians 1:19 may count him among the apostles, but readers differ on how to take the verse.
- **Junia, Andronicus**: Romans 16:7 can be read as well known among the apostles or well known to them; translations differ.
- **Stephen**: One of the seven chosen to serve (Acts 6:5), not an apostle.
- **Mary Magdalene**: Later writers called her apostle to the apostles, but the New Testament does not use the title.

### Near misses

- **Cat, cats**: The cat appears only in the Letter of Jeremiah (Baruch 6:22), which is outside the 66 books.
- **Elephant, elephants**: Ivory is mentioned (1 Kings 10:22), but the elephant itself is not named.
- **Rabbit, rabbits, bunny**: Close: Scripture's word is hare (Leviticus 11:6).
- **Dinosaur, dinosaurs, T rex, brontosaurus**: The Bible does not use that word. Job 40–41 describes behemoth and leviathan.
- **Cherub, cherubim, seraph, seraphim**: Heavenly beings rather than animals (Ezekiel 10:1; Isaiah 6:2).
- **Penguin, kangaroo, tiger, zebra, giraffe, panda**: A real animal, but not one named in the Bible.
- **Apple**: A fruit, not a creature.

| 🐑 The Lost Sheep (100) | 1 |

**🐑 The Lost Sheep:** Onesiphorus. Onesiphorus searched Rome for Paul in prison and often refreshed him, unashamed of his chains (2 Timothy 1:16–17).

**🪑 Best Seat:** Zacchaeus. Zacchaeus, a chief tax collector and short in stature, climbed a sycamore tree to see Jesus (Luke 19:2–4).

**🐑 The Lost Sheep:** Tekoa. Amos was among the herdsmen of Tekoa when the LORD took him from following the flock (Amos 1:1; 7:14–15).

**🪑 Best Seat:** Tarshish. Jonah boarded a ship for Tarshish to flee from the presence of the LORD (Jonah 1:3).

### Near misses

- **Vine and Branches, true vine**: One of the I am sayings (John 15:1–8), usually listed apart from the parables.
- **Ewe Lamb, Nathan**: That is a parable, but Nathan told it to David (2 Samuel 12:1–4).
- **Resurrection, his resurrection, empty tomb, Easter**: The greatest sign of all, but this prompt covers the miracles Jesus worked during his ministry.
- **Transfiguration, transfigured**: A revelation of his glory (Matthew 17:1–8), usually listed apart from his miracles.
- **Virgin birth, ascension**: A wonder of his life, but not a miracle he worked during his ministry.
- **Red Sea, manna, burning bush, plagues**: That belongs to the story of Moses.
- **Pentecost, tongues of fire**: That came after his ascension (Acts 2).
- **healed the sick, raised the dead, miracles**: That covers many miracles. Which one do you have in mind?

### Near misses

- **Lot's wife, Lots wife**: She looked back and became a pillar of salt (Genesis 19:26), but Scripture never gives her name.
- **Potiphar's wife, Potiphars wife**: She is in Genesis 39:7, but the text never gives her name.
- **Noah's wife, Noahs wife**: She went into the ark (Genesis 7:13), but Genesis never names her.
- **Job's wife, Jobs wife**: She speaks in Job 2:9, but is never named.
- **Samaritan woman, woman at the well**: One of the best-known women in the Gospels, but John never gives her name (John 4:7).
- **Veronica**: A name from later tradition. The Gospels do not name a Veronica.
- **Queen of Sheba**: She visited Solomon (1 Kings 10:1), but Scripture gives her title, not her name.
- **Pilate's wife, Pilates wife, Claudia Procula, Procula**: She sent Pilate a warning (Matthew 27:19), but the Gospel does not name her.
- **Mary Magdalene the prostitute, Magdalene prostitute, prostitute**: Scripture says seven demons had gone out of Mary Magdalene (Luke 8:2). It never calls her a prostitute.
- **Oholah, Aholah, Oholibah, Aholibah**: Ezekiel's names for Samaria and Jerusalem in a parable (Ezekiel 23:4), not women who lived.
- **Lilith**: Not a woman in Scripture. Isaiah 34:14 has a word some translations render "night creature".

**🐑 The Lost Sheep:** Man thrown into Elisha's grave. He is the only person in Scripture raised by touching a dead prophet's bones: he revived and stood up when his body touched Elisha's (2 Kings 13:21).

**🪑 Best Seat:** none

### 🍞 Five Loaves (30)

- **Tabitha** · Acts 9:36–41 · A disciple at Joppa, full of good works; Peter said, "Tabitha, get up!" *(manual)*<br><small>labels: Dorcas · anchor: Tabitha</small>

### Near misses

- **Widow's son, son of a widow, widow**: Two widows' sons were raised: at Zarephath through Elijah (1 Kings 17:22) and at Nain by Jesus (Luke 7:15). Name the town and cast again.
- **Elijah**: Elijah never died: he went up to heaven in a whirlwind (2 Kings 2:11).
- **Enoch**: Enoch never died: "he was not found, because God took him" (Genesis 5:24; Hebrews 11:5).
- **Samuel, Samuel at Endor, witch of Endor**: At Endor the medium saw Samuel come up (1 Samuel 28:11–14), but he was not raised to life again.
